prior_summary: Object-centric predictive relation conditioning: a shared two-object encoder and shared short-horizon relation forecaster expose object-to-TCP, object-to-goal, and inter-object structure to one learned action diffusion U-Net. Forecasts are supervised by demonstration futures during training and computed only from the two causal observations at deployment.
applicable_conditions: The full unstack_sort task from the initial red-on-blue stack through red placement, transition to blue, blue placement, and demonstrated release and retreat. Inputs are the supplied world-frame state history, including robot joints, both object poses, and both goals. Both object representations are always present; there is no externally selected skill or time-based phase schedule.
termination_guidance: The unchanged evaluator stops when red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal holds under its rotated-footprint and height tests, or at its physical step limit. This policy adds no release, clearance, velocity, or sustained-hold requirement. The forecast heads do not control termination, and the model can represent the demonstrated post-placement opening and retreat if queried.
limitations: The twelve demonstrations have a narrow initial stack-location distribution, fixed goals, nearly upright cubes, and a common manipulation order. Weight sharing and explicit relations are inductive biases, not guarantees of generalization. Deterministic relation forecasts may average ambiguous dwell transitions and are neither action-conditioned physics nor an inverse-kinematics solver. Absolute joint targets are not made equivariant by relative features. Only two observations are available; no hidden clock, persistent memory, hard grasp rule, or recovery controller is supplied. No rollout performance has been measured for design or selection.
